films.ov: Amid the sweltering summer heat in northern Argentina, two middle-class families retreat to a crumbling country estate and a modest townhouse, where strained relationships, simmering tensions, and the presence of children and servants quietly expose the fractures of family life. Between idle days, gossip, and unspoken desires, the boundaries of class, tradition, and faith are reflected in their everyday interactions.
After running into something with her car, Vero experiences a particular psychological state. She realizes she might have killed someone.

In a remote South American colony in the late 18th century, officer Zama of the Spanish crown waits in vain for a transfer to a more prestigious location. He suffers small humiliations and petty politicking as he increasingly succumbs to lust and paranoia.

Amalia is an adolescent girl who is caught in the throes of her emerging sexuality and her deeply held passion for her Catholic faith. These two drives mingle when the visiting Dr. Jano takes advantage of a crowd to get inappropriately close to the girl. Repulsed by him but inspired by an inner burning, Amalia decides it is her God-given mission to save the doctor from his behavior, and she begins to stalk Dr. Jano, becoming a most unusual voyeur.
A wife tries to leave her village to get away from her abusive husband.

martel.desc: An Argentine director from the northern province of Salta. Her films build a sense of decay and menace from overlapping sound and partial views.
martel.sig: Builds unease from sound and from what sits just outside the frame.
facts: Her first three features are set in Salta, her home region of Argentina.
Has said she thinks about a film's sound before its images.
lists: 3 films in the TSPDT 1,000 Greatest Films; the highest is La Ciénaga at #274.
4 films received votes in the 2022 Sight and Sound critics' poll; the highest is La Ciénaga at #119.

films.ov: John, an ambitious but undisciplined New York City office worker, meets and marries Mary. They start a family, struggle to cope with marital stress, financial setbacks, and tragedy, all while lost amid the anonymous, pitiless throngs of the big city.
An uncompromising, visionary architect struggles to maintain his integrity and individualism despite personal, professional and economic pressures to conform to popular standards.
Beautiful half-breed Pearl Chavez becomes the ward of her dead father's first love and finds herself torn between her sons, one good and the other bad.
The love story of young Countess Natasha Rostova and Count Pierre Bezukhov is interwoven with the Great Patriotic War of 1812 against Napoleon's invading army.

The story of an idle rich boy who joins the US Army's Rainbow Division and is sent to France to fight in World War I, becomes friends with two working class men, experiences the horrors of trench warfare, and finds love with a French girl.
A wandering cowboy gets caught up in a range war.

kingvidor.desc: His career ran from 1913 to 1959. The Crowd follows an ordinary clerk lost in the mass of the modern city, and his later films push emotion and landscape to extremes.
kingvidor.sig: Moved from silent social epics to fevered Technicolor melodrama.
facts: The Crowd used hidden cameras on New York streets.
Directed the Kansas scenes of The Wizard of Oz without credit.

films.ov: Once a young woman gets a man to fall in love with her, he must prove himself financially stable and meet her dowry requirements.
Pasquale and Maria, husband and wife, live in a palace supposedly haunted by ghosts and pay no rent. When Pasquale finds some food in the cupboard he thinks the ghosts are at work.

A young girl comes to prison and experiences the entire prison subculture. The inmates she befriends vary from big tough dangerous dames to smaller submissive ladies who are totally lost in prison life.
A lovely, incisive portrait of adolescents in the crowded San Giovanni quarter of Rome during the last years of WWII.

renatocastellani.desc: His comedies of young love among the poor kept the locations and amateur casts of neorealism and dropped its despair.
renatocastellani.sig: A founder of pink neorealism: neorealist methods with a lighter heart.
facts: Two Cents Worth of Hope cast non-professionals from a village near Naples.
Won the Golden Lion for his Romeo and Juliet in 1954.
lists: Won the top prize at Cannes for Two Cents Worth of Hope (1952, shared).

films.ov: In 1960s Poland, young novitiate Anna is on the verge of taking her vows when she discovers a family secret dating back to the years of the German occupation.
A man and a woman meet in the ruins of post-war Poland. With vastly different backgrounds and temperaments, they are fatally mismatched and yet drawn to each other.

In the Yorkshire countryside, working-class tomboy Mona meets the exotic, pampered Tamsin. To seal their friendship, Mona introduces Tamsin to her born-again Christian brother and helps her spy on her adulterous father. Bound together by their secrets, the two girls see their friendship deepen and...
An American writer moves to Paris to be closer to his daughter and finds himself falling immediately on hard times.
In 1949, German writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika embark on a road trip across a Germany in ruins, from US-dominated Frankfurt to Soviet-controlled Weimar.

Tanya leaves Moscow with her street-wise 10-year-old son Artiom to meet her English fiancée in London. But after he fails to turn up at the airport, Tanya, intent on staying in England, is forced to apply for political asylum and transferred to Stonehaven, a grimy former seaside resort where...

pawelpawlikowski.desc: He started in British documentary. His Polish films are framed in the Academy ratio, with characters placed low in the image, and tell decades in under ninety minutes.
pawelpawlikowski.sig: Compressed, black-and-white dramas of postwar Poland.
facts: Ida won the foreign-language Oscar, the first for a Polish film.
Won Best Director at Cannes for Cold War, which is loosely based on his parents.
awards: European Film Award for Best Director
European Film Award for Best Director
lists: 2 films received votes in the 2022 Sight and Sound critics' poll; the highest is Ida at #608.

films.ov: Filmmaker and artist Jack Smith described his own film as a “comedy set in a haunted movie studio.” Flaming Creatures begins humorously enough with several men and women, mostly of indeterminate gender, vamping it up in front of the camera and participating in a mock advertisement for an indelible, heart-shaped brand of lipstick. However, things take a dark, nightmarish turn when a transvestite chases, catches and begins molesting a woman. Soon, all of the titular “creatures” participate in a (mostly clothed) orgy that causes a massive earthquake. After the creatures are killed in the resulting chaos, a vampire dressed like an old Hollywood starlet rises from her coffin to resurrect the dead. All ends happily enough when the now undead creatures dance with each other, even though another orgy and earthquake loom over the end title card.

Shot in 1959, Scotch Tape is Jack Smith's first film -- a joyous, three-minute romp, in color, using Peter Duchin's rhumba "Carinhoso" for its soundtrack. Three young men merrily bop through the wreckage of razed buildings at the site of what would become Lincoln Center. Apparently, Scotch Tape was...

films.ov: Edie Bouvier Beale and her mother, Edith, two aging, eccentric relatives of Jackie Kennedy Onassis, are the sole inhabitants of a Long Island estate. The women reveal themselves to be misfits with outsized, engaging personalities. Much of the conversation is centered on their pasts, as mother and daughter now rarely leave home.

films.ov: A collection of Halloween-themed videotapes unleashes a series of twisted, blood-soaked tales, turning trick-or-treat into a struggle for survival.

Two women retreat to a lake house to get a break from the pressures of the outside world, only to realize how disconnected from each other they have become, allowing their suspicions to bleed into reality.

Anger rages in Philip as he awaits the publication of his second novel. He feels pushed out of his adopted home city by the constant crowds and noise, a deteriorating relationship with his photographer girlfriend Ashley, and his own indifference to promoting the novel. When Philip's idol Ike Zimmerman offers his isolated summer home as a refuge, he finally gets the peace and quiet to focus on his favorite subject: himself.
A self-destructive punk rocker struggles with sobriety while trying to recapture the creative inspiration that led her band to success.

An intersectional narrative of two families in Brooklyn and the unraveling of unspoken unhappiness that occurs when a young foreign girl spending time abroad upsets the balance on both sides.

alexrossperry.sig: Abrasive literary comedies about unpleasant people.

films.ov: "Selma," as in Alabama, the place where segregation in the South was at its worst, leading to a march that ended in violence, forcing a famous statement by President Lyndon B. Johnson that ultimately led to the signing of the Voting Rights Act.
After the disappearance of her scientist father, three peculiar beings send Meg, her brother, and her friend to space in order to find him.
An in-depth look at the prison system in the United States and how it reveals the nation's history of racial inequality.
While investigating the global phenomenon of caste and its dark influence on society, a journalist faces unfathomable personal loss and uncovers the beauty of human resilience.

When her husband is sentenced to eight years in prison, Ruby drops out of medical school in order to focus on her husband's well-being while he's incarcerated - leading her on a journey of self-discovery in the process.
Chronicles a day in the life of a grieving woman, and the twelve visitors who help her move forward.

August 28: A Day in the Life of a People
avaduvernay.desc: A former publicist whose films and series examine the civil rights movement and mass incarceration.
avaduvernay.sig: Historical drama and documentary about race and justice in America.
facts: Selma made her the first Black woman nominated for the Golden Globe for best director.
13th was nominated for the documentary Oscar.

films.ov: In an alternate present-day version of Oakland, black telemarketer Cassius Green discovers a magical key to professional success – which propels him into a macabre universe.
A group of shoplifters take aim at a cutthroat fashion maven by stealing from her stores and reselling them at a lower price — what they call 'fashion-forward philanthropy'.

bootsriley.desc: Frontman of the hip-hop group The Coup, he turned to film with a surreal comedy about telemarketing and labour.

facts: Fronts the hip-hop group The Coup.

films.ov: Twenty years removed from Alice Barlow's murder by a thief looking for her jewels, newlyweds Paul and Bella Mallen move into the very house where the crime was committed. Retired detective B.G. Rough, who worked on the Barlow case, is still in the area and grows suspicious of Paul, who he feels bears a striking resemblance to one of Barlow's relatives. Rough must find the truth before the killer can strike again and reclaim his bounty.
A czarist captain stops at nothing to learn the secrets of a countess rumored to have sold her soul to the devil in order to always win at cards.
In 1948, immediately before a ceasefire takes effect, four volunteers fighting for Israel are ordered to take Hill 24, overlooking the road to Jerusalem.
This tale of intrigue finds Valentina Cortese involved in an assassination plot. She helps the police apprehend the conspirators after an innocent bystander is accidentally killed.

thorolddickinson.desc: His Gaslight was suppressed by MGM to make way for its own remake, and The Queen of Spades became a cult film; he later founded the first university film department in Britain, at the Slade.
thorolddickinson.sig: A precise stylist of British gothic, and of the first British film-studies department.
facts: MGM bought the rights to his Gaslight and tried to destroy the prints before releasing George Cukor's version.

films.ov: A small town in Spain, October 1955. Isabel, a 35-year-old dreamer who feels like a failure because she is not married yet, becomes the new target of a group of soulless pranksters.
A couple has an affair strike a bicyclist with their car and don't offer aid out of fear of their relationship being exposed.
Chris Miller, living with her stepmother in a large secluded mansion, finds her isolation interrupted by the arrival of an unknown scythe-wielding killer.

Juan and Carmen are a humble couple living in Madrid. She does the housework and he works as an electrician in a film studio. Their dreams of wellness come true when they win a contest sponsored by a soap brand.

1865, The American Civil War: Five POW manage to escape by balloon from Fort Richmond. Caught in a storm and with the balloon damaged they find themselves 'shipwrecked' on a volcanic desert island somewhere in the Pacific. Just before crash landing their leader, the brilliant engineer Cyrus Smith...
A workshop employee decides to take advantage of a long weekend to go to Torremolinos to have fun and chat up foreign tourists.

juanantoniobardem.desc: With Luis García Berlanga he set out to renew Spanish cinema, making Death of a Cyclist and Main Street, stories of guilt and provincial hypocrisy; he was arrested during the shooting of the latter.
juanantoniobardem.sig: A communist director who criticised Franco's Spain from inside it.
facts: Death of a Cyclist won the FIPRESCI Prize at Cannes in 1955.
His nephew is the actor Javier Bardem.

films.ov: Lisbon, 1989. A middle-aged poor man, tormented by an illness, lives in a cheap room in a family boarding house, in the old section of the city's waterfront.
An ice-cream seller lusts after the female employees in his shop.
After receiving a visit from a messenger of God, João de Deus wins his buddy's girlfriend through a roll of the dice.

Laura Rossellini, a widow from Rome, vacations on the Algarve coast one hot summer. One day while sunbathing, she finds a wounded man named Robert drifting in the surf on a rubber raft. She takes him home, and, after he is revived, learns his story. As they talk, their mutual attraction grows,...

joaocesarmonteiro.sig: Portuguese cinema's scandalous poet, playing his own lecherous alter ego.

films.ov: Murderesses Velma Kelly and Roxie Hart find themselves on death row together and fight for the fame that will keep them from the gallows in 1920s Chicago.

In a woods filled with magic and fairy tale characters, a baker and his wife set out to end the curse put on them by their neighbor, a spiteful witch.
Mary Poppins returns to the Banks family and helps them evade grave dangers by taking them on magical, musical adventures.
In the years before World War II, a penniless Japanese child is torn from her family to work as a maid in a geisha house.

The youngest of King Triton’s daughters, and the most defiant, Ariel longs to find out more about the world beyond the sea, and while visiting the surface, falls for the dashing Prince Eric. With mermaids forbidden to interact with humans, Ariel makes a deal with the evil sea witch, Ursula, which...

robmarshall.desc: A stage director and choreographer whose Chicago stages its songs as the heroine's fantasies, followed by Nine, Into the Woods and Mary Poppins Returns.
robmarshall.sig: A Broadway choreographer who directed the film of Chicago.
facts: Chicago was the first musical to win Best Picture since Oliver! in 1968.
Directed Memoirs of a Geisha (2005).

films.t: All Quiet on the Western Front
films.ov: Paul Baumer and his friends Albert and Muller, egged on by romantic dreams of heroism, voluntarily enlist in the German army. Full of excitement and patriotic fervour, the boys enthusiastically march into a war they believe in. But once on the Western Front, they discover the soul-destroying horror of World War I.

After the unexpected death of the Pope, Cardinal Lawrence is tasked with managing the covert and ancient ritual of electing a new one. Sequestered in the Vatican with the Catholic Church’s most powerful leaders until the process is complete, Lawrence finds himself at the center of a conspiracy that could lead to its downfall.
Amid the glittering casinos of Macau, a gambler running from his past—and his debts—becomes fascinated by an enigmatic woman at the baccarat table.

Ten-year-old Jack has to take care of his little brother, six-year-old Manuel, every day from the time he gets up to the time he goes to bed. When Manuel suffers an accident, their lives change forever.

edwardberger.desc: A German director from television whose All Quiet on the Western Front, the first German-language film of Remarque's novel, won four Oscars; he followed it with Conclave.
